title: Surface cancelable streams and centralize retry shim for SDK parity
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduce cancelable stream primitives across SDKs; centralize retry decision logic into shared retry-shim; bump SDK versions (Python 2.6.0, TypeScript 1.9.0, Go v0.8.0). Backwards compatible: opt-in helpers; no forced client changes.
description:
Motivation: We continue to see client libraries re-implementing similar streaming lifecycle and retry behavior (token refresh during long-lived streams, cancellation propagation, and duplicate backoff strategies). This PR introduces a lightweight, SDK-friendly CancelableStream abstraction and moves retry decision & backoff logic into a shared retry-shim (redwood/sdk-shared/retry) so Python/TS/Go SDKs can converge on identical semantics without duplicating fragile state machines.

What this PR changes (single-string summary): Adds CancelableStream helpers and context-aware wrappers for streaming endpoints; centralizes retry/backoff/token-refresh decisions in a shared shim used by all three SDKs; small ergonomics helpers (WithContext, StreamCloseNotify); updates examples and tests; bumps client versions.

Checklist: - [x] Design proposal landed in ENG-1423 - [x] Core retry-shim implemented and unit-tested - [x] Python/TS/Go bindings added to call into shim - [x] End-to-end streaming smoke tests updated - [x] Docs snippets refreshed - [x] Version bumps for each SDK

Commits (high level): - feat(retry-shim): introduce shared retry decision module and deterministic backoff profiles - feat(streams): add CancelableStream interface and WithContext helpers in sdk-shared - feat(go-sdk): wire CancelableStream adapter, expose Stream.CloseNotify and Stream.Cancel - feat(py-sdk): add StreamingClient.with_cancelable() helper and token refresh hook during retries - feat(ts-sdk): expose makeCancelableStream and typed iterator wrapper - test: add cross-sdk streaming integration harness (flaky-test guard) - docs: update streaming.md and quickstarts

Files changed (high level): - redwood/sdk-shared/retry/* (new): core retry logic, backoff profiles, token-refresh orchestration hooks - redwood/sdk-shared/stream/* (new): CancelableStream interface, context bindings, utilities - redwood/sdk-go/streaming.go: adapter and exported helpers - redwood/sdk-python/streaming.py: convenience wrappers and small refactor to client handshake - redwood/sdk-typescript/streams.ts: typed iterable wrapper and cancellation token doc examples - docs/quickstarts/streaming.md: replace example with WithContext-using pattern - tests/e2e/streaming_harness: add cross-sdk test case simulating token rotation and mid-stream cancellation

Notes on ergonomics and compatibility: The CancelableStream API is opt-in: existing streaming calls continue to return the older iterator/async-iterator shape. New convenience constructors (e.g. client.stream().as_cancelable(ctx)) provide an ergonomic migration path. The retry-shim exposes a minimal interface (shouldRetry(error, attemptMetadata) -> {decision, backoffMs, refreshToken}) so SDK tongues can keep language-idiomatic wrappers.

Review conversation (abridged, single string): Ethan Cole (reviewer): "Great consolidation. Two asks: make backoff profiles pluggable and add metrics hooks when retry-shim triggers token refresh." Priya (author): "Pluggable profiles added behind RetryConfig; metrics hooks exposed via RetryHooks interface; added tests." Marta Puig (reviewer): "Please ensure TS iterator typings remain compatible for downstream consumers; watch for runtime-heavy allocations in Go." Priya: "TS tests updated to preserve Iterator<T> shape; Go implementation uses a single goroutine with channel-based streaming to avoid allocations on each token and includes microbench." Liu Zhang (final approver): "Tests and CI green; behavior verified by streaming canary locally. Approving for merge."

CI and stability: Initial CI run failed on a flaky e2e that simulates mid-stream token rotations (timeout). I reworked the harness to use deterministic fake-time and retried. Final CI: all checks pass (unit, linters, cross-sdk integration). Post-merge canary run against perf lane showed no regression in median latency for typical 1-2s streams; tail latency improvement in high retry scenarios due to centralized token refresh queuing.

Merge: Squash merge after approvals. Merge commit records authorship and links to ENG-1423/ENG-1668.

Migration guidance for SDK consumers (short): 1) No immediate action required. 2) To opt into cancellable streams, call the new helper on the client: e.g. py: client.stream(...).as_cancelable(context) or ts: makeCancelableStream(client.stream(...), abortSignal). 3) If you implement custom retry policies, switch to RetryConfig to maintain compatibility.

Follow-ups planned: - ENG-1668: metrics instrumentation for retry events and token-refresh counts - Small perf pass to reduce allocation overhead in the Go adapter - Docs: add migration guide and a short video showing cancelation + graceful shutdown

Related: ENG-1423, ENG-1668, and a related internal incident INT-3021 (token-rotation causing duplicate in-flight refreshes).

add cancelable stream interface and language adapters
python: add as_cancelable and token refresh integration
typescript: typed iterator wrapper and abortSignal integration
go: channel-based cancelable stream adapter and microbench fixes
tests: cross-sdk streaming harness and flaky guards
